label: Exercise
note: Guide mapping for /exercise/?q=<id>. Aliases are matched against plan text (lowercased, punctuation removed, whole words, optional plural).

dumbbell-row.name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Row
dumbbell-row.summary: A hinged pulling exercise that strengthens the upper back.

photos.caption: Starting position
photos.alt: Bent-Over Dumbbell Row: starting position

photos.caption: Finishing position
photos.alt: Bent-Over Dumbbell Row: finishing position

steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward from your hips with a flat back and soft knees.
Let the dumbbells hang straight down below your shoulders.
Breathe out and pull the dumbbells toward your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your back flat and neck neutral.
Lead with your elbows; avoid shrugging your shoulders toward your ears.

bird-dog.name: Bird Dog
bird-dog.summary: An all-fours exercise that trains the core and back muscles to keep the spine stable.

photos.caption: Arm and opposite leg extended
photos.alt: Bird Dog: arm and opposite leg extended

photos.caption: Holding a long, level line
photos.alt: Bird Dog: holding a long, level line

steps: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace your stomach so your back stays flat.
Slowly reach your right arm forward and your left leg back until both are level with your body.
Hold for a breath, then return to the start with control.
Repeat with the left arm and right leg; that is one rep per side.
tips: Imagine balancing a glass of water on your lower back — don't let it tip.
Reach long rather than high; lifting too far arches the back.

bodyweight-squat.name: Bodyweight Squat
bodyweight-squat.summary: The basic sit-and-stand pattern that builds strength in the legs and hips.

photos.caption: Standing tall
photos.alt: Bodyweight Squat: standing tall

photos.caption: Bottom of the squat
photos.alt: Bodyweight Squat: bottom of the squat

steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
Brace your stomach and push your hips back as if sitting into a chair.
Bend your knees and lower until your thighs are about parallel with the floor, or as low as is comfortable.
Keep your chest up and your heels on the floor.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up, breathing out as you rise.
tips: Let your knees track in line with your toes rather than caving inward.
Squat to a chair or bench if you need a depth target.

bridge-march.name: Bridge March
bridge-march.summary: A glute bridge where you lift one foot at a time, adding a balance and core challenge.

photos.caption: One leg lifted while holding the bridge
photos.alt: Bridge March: one leg lifted while holding the bridge

photos.caption: Lifted leg extended
photos.alt: Bridge March: lifted leg extended

steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, then lift your hips into a glute bridge.
Keeping your hips level, lift your right foot a few centimetres and bring the knee toward your chest.
Place the foot back down and repeat with the left leg.
Keep alternating for the planned reps without letting your hips drop.
Lower your hips to the floor to finish.
tips: Move slowly; the goal is to keep your pelvis still while each leg lifts.
Hold a plain glute bridge first if your hips sag.

cable-bicep-curl.name: Cable Bicep Curl
cable-bicep-curl.summary: A bicep curl on the low pulley that keeps the muscle under tension through the whole movement.

photos.caption: Starting position
photos.alt: Cable Bicep Curl: starting position

photos.caption: Finishing position
photos.alt: Cable Bicep Curl: finishing position

steps: Attach a straight bar to the low pulley and set a light weight.
Hold the bar with palms facing up, hands shoulder-width apart, and step back so the cable is taut.
Keep your elbows at your sides and curl the bar up toward your chest while breathing out.
Squeeze at the top, then lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your upper arms still; only the forearms should move.
In interval work, keep a steady rhythm for the full minute rather than rushing early reps.

glute-kickback.name: Cable Glute Kickback
glute-kickback.summary: A standing kickback that isolates the glutes.

photos.caption: Starting position
photos.alt: Cable Glute Kickback: starting position

photos.caption: Finishing position
photos.alt: Cable Glute Kickback: finishing position

steps: Attach an ankle strap to the low pulley and fasten it around one ankle.
Face the machine, hold it for support and hinge forward slightly.
Squeeze your glute and push the strapped leg straight back.
Pause, then return slowly. Finish the reps and switch legs.
tips: Keep your back flat — the movement comes from the hip, not the lower back.
Keep the standing knee slightly bent.

leg-curl.name: Cable Leg Curl
leg-curl.summary: A single-leg curl that isolates the hamstrings.

facts.Equipment: Cable machine with ankle strap, or leg curl machine

photos.caption: Starting position
photos.alt: Cable Leg Curl: starting position

photos.caption: Finishing position
photos.alt: Cable Leg Curl: finishing position

steps: Attach an ankle strap to the low pulley and fasten it around one ankle.
Face the machine and hold it for support, standing tall.
Breathe out and bend the knee to curl your heel toward your glutes.
Pause, then lower slowly. Finish the reps and switch legs.
tips: Keep your thighs in line; only the lower leg should move.
Use a light weight and control both directions.

tricep-pushdown.name: Cable Tricep Pushdown
tricep-pushdown.summary: A cable exercise that isolates the triceps.

facts.Equipment: Cable machine with bar or rope

photos.caption: Starting position
photos.alt: Cable Tricep Pushdown: starting position

photos.caption: Finishing position
photos.alt: Cable Tricep Pushdown: finishing position

steps: Attach a bar or rope to the high pulley and stand facing it.
Hold the attachment with elbows bent and tucked at your sides.
Breathe out and push down until your arms are straight.
Pause, then let the attachment rise slowly until your forearms are just above parallel.
tips: Keep your elbows pinned at your sides.
Stand tall and avoid leaning over the weight.

cat-cow.name: Cat-Cow Stretch
cat-cow.summary: A gentle flow between rounding and arching the spine to loosen the back.

photos.caption: Cat — back rounded
photos.alt: Cat-Cow Stretch: cat — back rounded

photos.caption: Cow — back gently arched
photos.alt: Cat-Cow Stretch: cow — back gently arched

steps: Start on hands and knees with a flat back.
Breathe in and let your stomach sink, lifting your chest and tailbone (cow).
Breathe out and round your back toward the ceiling, tucking your chin and tailbone (cat).
Move slowly between the two positions with your breath for the planned time.
tips: Move within a comfortable range; this is a mobility drill, not a stretch to force.
Keep your arms straight and weight evenly spread between hands and knees.

chest-opener-stretch.name: Chest Opener Stretch
chest-opener-stretch.summary: A standing stretch that opens the chest and the front of the shoulders.

photos.caption: Holding a stick at hip height
photos.alt: Chest Opener Stretch: holding a stick at hip height

photos.caption: Lifting to open the chest
photos.alt: Chest Opener Stretch: lifting to open the chest

steps: Stand tall and clasp your hands behind your back, or hold a stick or towel with a wide grip.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and lift your chest.
Gently raise your arms until you feel a stretch across your chest and shoulders.
Hold for the planned time, breathing slowly.
tips: Keep your ribs down; don't over-arch your lower back.
Use a wider grip on the stick if the stretch feels too strong.

childs-pose.name: Child's Pose
childs-pose.summary: A resting stretch for the back, hips and shoulders.

photos.caption: Sitting back toward the heels
photos.alt: Child's Pose: sitting back toward the heels

photos.caption: Resting forward into the pose
photos.alt: Child's Pose: resting forward into the pose

steps: Kneel on a mat with big toes together and knees hip-width apart.
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Walk your hands forward and lower your chest toward the floor, resting your forehead on the mat.
Breathe slowly into your back and hold for the planned time.
tips: Place a cushion under your hips or forehead if they don't reach.
Widen your knees for more room if your stomach feels compressed.

shoulder-stretch.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
shoulder-stretch.summary: A simple stretch for the back of the shoulder and upper back.

photos.caption: Standing tall
photos.alt: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch: standing tall

photos.caption: Arm drawn across the chest
photos.alt: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch: arm drawn across the chest

steps: Stand or sit tall with shoulders relaxed.
Bring one arm straight across your chest.
Use the other hand to gently press the arm closer to your chest, just above the elbow.
Hold for the planned time, then switch arms.
tips: Keep the stretched shoulder down, away from your ear.
Press on the upper arm, not the elbow joint.

dead-bug.name: Dead Bug
dead-bug.summary: A back-lying core exercise that teaches you to move your limbs while keeping the lower back still.

photos.caption: Arms and legs raised
photos.alt: Dead Bug: arms and legs raised

photos.caption: Opposite arm and leg lowered
photos.alt: Dead Bug: opposite arm and leg lowered

steps: Lie on your back with arms pointing to the ceiling and knees bent to 90° above your hips.
Press your lower back gently into the floor.
Slowly lower your right arm overhead and straighten your left leg toward the floor.
Stop just before your lower back lifts, then return to the start.
Repeat on the other side and keep alternating.
tips: Breathe out as you extend your arm and leg.
Keep the range small at first; control matters more than distance.

deep-breathing.name: Deep Breathing
deep-breathing.summary: Slow belly breathing to calm the nervous system and aid recovery.

photos.caption: Seated in a comfortable position
photos.alt: Deep Breathing: seated in a comfortable position

photos.caption: How the diaphragm moves as you breathe
photos.alt: Deep Breathing: how the diaphragm moves as you breathe

steps: Sit comfortably or lie down with one hand on your chest and one on your stomach.
Breathe in slowly through your nose for about four seconds, letting your stomach rise.
Pause briefly.
Breathe out through your mouth for about six seconds, letting your stomach fall.
Repeat for the planned time, keeping the hand on your chest fairly still.
tips: Longer out-breaths than in-breaths help the body relax.
If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing for a moment.

downward-dog.name: Downward Dog
downward-dog.summary: A yoga pose that stretches the hamstrings and calves while strengthening the shoulders.

photos.caption: Hips lifted, body in an inverted V
photos.alt: Downward Dog: hips lifted, body in an inverted V

photos.caption: Heels reaching toward the floor
photos.alt: Downward Dog: heels reaching toward the floor

steps: Start on hands and knees with hands slightly in front of your shoulders.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back, straightening your legs as much as is comfortable.
Press the floor away with your hands and let your head hang between your arms.
Hold, breathing slowly, and let your heels sink toward the floor.
tips: Bend your knees if your back rounds; a long spine matters more than straight legs.
Spread your fingers wide to share the load through your hands.

dumbbell-bicep-curl.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
dumbbell-bicep-curl.summary: A simple elbow-bending lift that builds the front of the upper arm.

photos.caption: Starting position
photos.alt: Dumbbell Bicep Curl: starting position

photos.caption: Finishing position
photos.alt: Dumbbell Bicep Curl: finishing position

steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight and palms facing forward.
Pin your elbows to your sides and brace your stomach lightly.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells toward your shoulders, moving only your forearms.
Pause for a moment at the top and squeeze the biceps.
Breathe in and lower the weights slowly until your arms are straight again.
tips: Don't swing your back or hips to lift the weight; choose a lighter dumbbell instead.
Lower the weight more slowly than you lift it — about two to three seconds.

dumbbell-chest-press.name: Dumbbell Chest Press
dumbbell-chest-press.summary: A pressing exercise on a bench that builds the chest, shoulders and triceps.

facts.Equipment: Pair of dumbbells and flat bench

photos.caption: Dumbbells lowered to chest level
photos.alt: Dumbbell Chest Press: dumbbells lowered to chest level

photos.caption: Dumbbells pressed up
photos.alt: Dumbbell Chest Press: dumbbells pressed up

steps: Lie on a flat bench with feet on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand at chest level.
Turn your palms to face your feet, elbows about 45° from your body.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells up until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower them slowly back to chest level.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades pulled back against the bench.
Choose a weight you can lower with control — no bouncing.

dumbbell-deadlift.name: Dumbbell Deadlift
dumbbell-deadlift.summary: A hip-hinge lift that builds the hamstrings, glutes and back.

photos.caption: Starting position
photos.alt: Dumbbell Deadlift: starting position

photos.caption: Finishing position
photos.alt: Dumbbell Deadlift: finishing position

steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Keep a slight bend in your knees and brace your core.
Push your hips back and lower the dumbbells along your legs, keeping your back flat.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings (around mid-shin).
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes at the top.
tips: Keep the weights close to your legs throughout.
Your back should stay flat — stop lowering before it starts to round.

dumbbell-lunge.name: Dumbbell Lunge
dumbbell-lunge.summary: A split-stance step that builds single-leg strength and balance.

photos.caption: Standing with dumbbells
photos.alt: Dumbbell Lunge: standing with dumbbells

photos.caption: Lowered into the lunge
photos.alt: Dumbbell Lunge: lowered into the lunge

steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Take a long step forward with one leg.
Lower your hips until both knees are bent to about 90°, back knee hovering above the floor.
Push through the front heel to return to standing.
Complete the planned reps on one leg, then switch (or alternate legs).
tips: Keep your front knee over your ankle, not drifting past your toes.
Practise without weights first if you feel unsteady.

dumbbell-shoulder-press.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
dumbbell-shoulder-press.summary: A pressing movement that strengthens the shoulders and upper arms.

facts.Equipment: Pair of dumbbells, bench with back support

photos.caption: Starting position
photos.alt: Dumbbell Shoulder Press: starting position

photos.caption: Finishing position
photos.alt: Dumbbell Shoulder Press: finishing position

steps: Sit on an upright bench with your back against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
Raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, palms facing forward and elbows below your wrists.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are nearly straight.
Pause, then lower them slowly back to shoulder height.
tips: Keep your lower back against the pad; don't arch to push the weight up.
Stop just short of locking the elbows at the top.

dumbbell-side-bend.name: Dumbbell Side Bend
dumbbell-side-bend.summary: A standing side-bend that strengthens the obliques.

photos.caption: Bending toward the dumbbell
photos.alt: Dumbbell Side Bend: bending toward the dumbbell

photos.caption: Returning upright
photos.alt: Dumbbell Side Bend: returning upright

steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in one hand and the other hand on your hip or behind your head.
Bend sideways toward the dumbbell, sliding it down your leg.
Use your opposite side's obliques to return upright.
Complete the planned reps, then switch hands.
tips: Bend directly sideways — don't twist or lean forward.
Use a moderate weight; heavy weights shift the work away from your waist.

sumo-squat.name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
sumo-squat.summary: A wide-stance squat that puts more work into the inner thighs and glutes.

photos.caption: Starting position
photos.alt: Dumbbell Sumo Squat: starting position

photos.caption: Finishing position
photos.alt: Dumbbell Sumo Squat: finishing position

steps: Stand with feet wide apart and toes pointed out about 45°.
Hold one dumbbell with both hands at arm's length between your legs.
Bend your knees and lower your hips straight down, keeping your back upright.
Pause when your thighs are near parallel, then push back up and squeeze your glutes at the top.
tips: Push your knees out in line with your toes.
Keep your torso upright rather than leaning forward.

foam-rolling.name: Foam Rolling
foam-rolling.summary: Self-massage with a foam roller to ease muscle tightness after training.

photos.caption: Rolling the front of the thighs
photos.alt: Foam Rolling: rolling the front of the thighs

photos.caption: Rolling the lower back area
photos.alt: Foam Rolling: rolling the lower back area

steps: Place the roller under the muscle you want to target, such as the front of your thighs.
Support yourself with your hands or forearms and roll slowly along the muscle.
When you find a tender spot, pause for 20–30 seconds and breathe.
Move on to the next area for the planned time.
tips: Avoid rolling directly over joints or bones.
No roller? Use your hands or a tennis ball for gentle self-massage.

full-body-stretch.name: Full-Body Stretch
full-body-stretch.summary: A gentle sequence of standing stretches to finish a session or ease stiffness.

photos.caption: Reaching overhead
photos.alt: Full-Body Stretch: reaching overhead

photos.caption: Side stretch
photos.alt: Full-Body Stretch: side stretch

steps: Reach both arms overhead and stretch tall for a few breaths.
Lean gently to each side to stretch along your ribs.
Fold forward with soft knees to stretch the back of your legs.
Add shoulder, chest and calf stretches, holding each for about 20–30 seconds.
Continue for the planned time, breathing slowly.
tips: Hold each stretch steadily without bouncing.
Aim for a gentle pull, never pain.

glute-bridge.name: Glute Bridge
glute-bridge.summary: A floor exercise that strengthens the glutes and supports a healthy lower back.

photos.caption: Lying with knees bent
photos.alt: Glute Bridge: lying with knees bent

photos.caption: Hips lifted into the bridge
photos.alt: Glute Bridge: hips lifted into the bridge

steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, arms by your sides.
Press through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips.
Rise until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Hold for a second at the top, then lower slowly to the floor.
tips: Lift with your glutes, not by arching your lower back.
Keep your knees pointing forward, not falling in or out.

goblet-squat.name: Goblet Squat
goblet-squat.summary: A squat holding one weight at the chest, which encourages an upright posture.

photos.caption: Standing with the dumbbell at the chest
photos.alt: Goblet Squat: standing with the dumbbell at the chest

photos.caption: Bottom of the squat
photos.alt: Goblet Squat: bottom of the squat

steps: Hold one end of a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands.
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out a little.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower between your legs, keeping your chest tall.
Go as low as you can while keeping your heels down, elbows inside your knees.
Drive through your feet to stand up, breathing out on the way up.
tips: Keep the dumbbell close to your chest throughout.
In timed intervals, pick a pace you can hold with good form for the whole minute.

hamstring-stretch.name: Hamstring Stretch
hamstring-stretch.summary: A stretch for the back of the thighs, done standing or seated.

photos.caption: Standing version — folding toward the toes
photos.alt: Hamstring Stretch: standing version — folding toward the toes

photos.caption: Seated version — reaching for one foot
photos.alt: Hamstring Stretch: seated version — reaching for one foot

steps: Standing: place one heel slightly in front of you with toes up, or stand with feet together.
Keep your back long and hinge forward from your hips until you feel a stretch behind the thigh.
Seated: sit with one leg straight and the other bent, foot against the inner thigh, then reach toward the straight leg's foot.
Hold the stretch for the planned time, breathing slowly, then switch legs.
tips: Stretch to mild tension only — never to pain.
Keep a slight bend in the knee if you feel pulling behind the knee joint.

mobility-circles.name: Joint Mobility Circles
mobility-circles.summary: Gentle circles for the arms, shoulders, hips and ankles to warm up joints and ease stiffness.

photos.caption: Arm circles
photos.alt: Joint Mobility Circles: arm circles

photos.caption: Shoulder circles
photos.alt: Joint Mobility Circles: shoulder circles

photos.caption: Hip circles on one leg
photos.alt: Joint Mobility Circles: hip circles on one leg

steps: Arm circles: hold your arms out to the sides and draw small circles, gradually making them bigger, then reverse.
Shoulder circles: roll your shoulders up, back and down in slow circles, then reverse.
Hip circles: stand on one leg (hold a wall if needed), lift the other knee and draw circles with it, then switch.
Ankle circles: lift one foot and slowly circle the ankle in each direction, then switch.
Complete the planned reps for each movement.
tips: Move slowly and stay within a pain-free range.
These work well as a warm-up before strength sessions.

hip-flexor-stretch.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
hip-flexor-stretch.summary: A half-kneeling stretch for the front of the hip, which tightens with long periods of sitting.

photos.caption: Half-kneeling
photos.alt: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch: half-kneeling

photos.caption: Shifting forward into the stretch
photos.alt: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch: shifting forward into the stretch

steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot in front, both knees at about 90°.
Tuck your tailbone and squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg.
Shift your hips gently forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip.
Hold for the planned time, then switch sides.
tips: Put a folded towel under your knee for comfort.
Keep your torso upright; don't arch your lower back.

knees-to-chest.name: Knees-to-Chest Stretch
knees-to-chest.summary: A lying stretch that gently releases the lower back.

photos.caption: Lying with knees bent
photos.alt: Knees-to-Chest Stretch: lying with knees bent

photos.caption: Hugging the knees to the chest
photos.alt: Knees-to-Chest Stretch: hugging the knees to the chest

steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Bring one knee, then the other, toward your chest.
Hold behind your thighs or over your shins and draw your knees gently closer.
Hold for the planned time, breathing slowly; rock gently side to side if it feels good.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Hold behind the thighs if holding the shins puts pressure on your knees.

leg-raise.name: Lying Leg Raise
leg-raise.summary: A lying exercise that works the lower abdominals.

photos.caption: Legs lowered
photos.alt: Lying Leg Raise: legs lowered

photos.caption: Legs raised
photos.alt: Lying Leg Raise: legs raised

steps: Lie on your back with legs straight and hands under your hips or by your sides.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Breathe out and raise your legs until they point toward the ceiling.
Lower slowly, stopping before your lower back lifts.
tips: Bend your knees to make it easier.
Move slowly; don't let the legs drop.

windshield-wiper.name: Lying Windshield Wipers
windshield-wiper.summary: A lying twist where the legs sway side to side, working the obliques and easing the spine.

photos.caption: Knees lowered to one side
photos.alt: Lying Windshield Wipers: knees lowered to one side

photos.caption: Legs lowered to one side
photos.alt: Lying Windshield Wipers: legs lowered to one side

steps: Lie on your back with arms out to the sides and knees bent above your hips.
Keep your shoulders on the floor and slowly lower both knees to one side.
Use your stomach muscles to bring them back to the centre.
Lower to the other side; one side and back is one rep.
For more challenge, straighten your legs.
tips: Only lower as far as you can while keeping both shoulders down.
Breathe out as you bring the legs back to the centre.

mountain-climber.name: Mountain Climbers
mountain-climber.summary: A plank-based movement that combines core work with light cardio.

photos.caption: High plank with one knee driven forward
photos.alt: Mountain Climbers: high plank with one knee driven forward

photos.caption: Switching legs
photos.alt: Mountain Climbers: switching legs

steps: Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders.
Bring your right knee toward your chest.
Return it and bring the left knee forward.
Keep alternating at the planned pace — slow and controlled to start.
tips: Keep your hips level with your shoulders.
Slow pace works the core more; faster pace adds cardio.

outdoor-walk.name: Outdoor Walk
outdoor-walk.summary: An easy walk outdoors for active recovery and fresh air.

photos.caption: Walking at a comfortable pace
photos.alt: Outdoor Walk: walking at a comfortable pace

photos.caption: Easy stride outdoors
photos.alt: Outdoor Walk: easy stride outdoors

steps: Wear comfortable shoes and pick a safe, familiar route.
Start at an easy pace for the first few minutes.
Walk at a comfortable pace for the planned time, swinging your arms naturally.
Slow down for the last couple of minutes.
tips: Carry water on warm days.
This is a recovery walk — you should finish feeling refreshed, not tired.

pelvic-tilt.name: Pelvic Tilt
pelvic-tilt.summary: A small floor movement that wakes up the deep core and eases the lower back.

photos.caption: Lying with knees bent
photos.alt: Pelvic Tilt: lying with knees bent

photos.caption: Tilting the pelvis and lifting slightly
photos.alt: Pelvic Tilt: tilting the pelvis and lifting slightly

steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Breathe out and gently flatten your lower back into the floor by tilting your pelvis upward.
Hold for two to three seconds.
Breathe in and release back to a neutral position.
tips: The movement is small — think of tucking your tailbone.
Keep your glutes and shoulders relaxed; the work comes from the lower stomach.

plank.name: Plank
plank.summary: A static hold that teaches the core to keep the spine steady.

photos.caption: Setting up on the forearms
photos.alt: Plank: setting up on the forearms

photos.caption: Holding the plank
photos.alt: Plank: holding the plank

steps: Kneel on a mat and place your forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders.
Step your feet back one at a time until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Tighten your stomach and glutes as if bracing for a light poke in the belly.
Hold the position for the planned time while breathing slowly and steadily.
Lower your knees to the mat to finish.
tips: Don't let your hips sag or rise; picture a straight plank of wood.
If your form breaks, rest on your knees and restart rather than holding a sagging plank.

plank-shoulder-tap.name: Plank with Shoulder Taps
plank-shoulder-tap.summary: A high plank where you lift one hand at a time, training the core to resist twisting.

photos.caption: High plank position
photos.alt: Plank with Shoulder Taps: high plank position
photos.credit: U.S. Army 10AAMDC by Sgt. Yesenia Cadavid

photos.caption: Tapping the opposite shoulder
photos.alt: Plank with Shoulder Taps: tapping the opposite shoulder
photos.credit: U.S. Army 10AAMDC by Sgt. Yesenia Cadavid

steps: Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and feet slightly wider than hip-width.
Brace your stomach and glutes so your body is a straight line.
Lift your right hand and tap your left shoulder, then return the hand to the floor.
Repeat with the left hand to the right shoulder; each tap counts as one rep.
Keep alternating at a slow, controlled pace.
tips: Keep your hips level; avoid rocking side to side as each hand lifts.
Widen your feet to make it easier, or bring them closer for a greater challenge.

quad-stretch.name: Quadriceps Stretch
quad-stretch.summary: A stretch for the front of the thigh.

photos.caption: Lying version with a strap
photos.alt: Quadriceps Stretch: lying version with a strap

photos.caption: Side-lying version
photos.alt: Quadriceps Stretch: side-lying version

steps: Standing: hold a wall for balance, bend one knee and hold the ankle behind you.
Lying on your side: bend the top knee and hold the ankle, or loop a strap around it.
Gently draw the heel toward your glutes while keeping your knees close together.
Hold for the planned time, then switch legs.
tips: Tuck your tailbone slightly to feel the stretch higher up the thigh.
Avoid pulling the heel hard into the glutes if your knee feels strained.

russian-twist.name: Russian Twist
russian-twist.summary: A seated rotation that works the obliques and deep core.

photos.caption: Leaning back with weight centred
photos.alt: Russian Twist: leaning back with weight centred

photos.caption: Rotating to the side
photos.alt: Russian Twist: rotating to the side

steps: Sit with knees bent and heels on the floor.
Lean back slightly with a long, straight spine and hold your hands (or a light weight) at your chest.
Rotate your torso to one side, then through the centre to the other side.
Each turn to a side counts as one rep; keep breathing steadily.
tips: Rotate through your ribs and shoulders, not just your arms.
Keep your feet on the floor until you can keep a straight back throughout.

cable-row.name: Seated Cable Row
cable-row.summary: A pulling exercise that strengthens the upper back and supports good posture.

photos.caption: Starting position
photos.alt: Seated Cable Row: starting position

photos.caption: Finishing position
photos.alt: Seated Cable Row: finishing position

steps: Sit at the cable row station with feet on the platform and knees slightly bent.
Hold the handle with arms extended and sit tall.
Breathe out and pull the handle toward your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause, then extend your arms slowly to return.
tips: Keep your torso still; don't rock back to pull the weight.
Lead with your elbows and keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.

seated-forward-fold.name: Seated Forward Fold
seated-forward-fold.summary: A seated stretch for the hamstrings and back of the body.

photos.caption: Reaching toward the feet
photos.alt: Seated Forward Fold: reaching toward the feet

photos.caption: Folding over straight legs
photos.alt: Seated Forward Fold: folding over straight legs

steps: Sit on a mat with legs straight in front of you and feet flexed.
Sit up tall and breathe in.
Breathe out and hinge forward from your hips, reaching toward your shins, ankles or feet.
Hold where you feel a gentle stretch, breathing slowly for the planned time.
Roll up slowly to sit tall again.
tips: Bend your knees slightly if your lower back rounds a lot.
Lead with your chest rather than pulling your head toward your knees.

seated-spinal-twist.name: Seated Spinal Twist
seated-spinal-twist.summary: A seated rotation that eases stiffness in the back and hips.

photos.caption: Twisting over the bent knee
photos.alt: Seated Spinal Twist: twisting over the bent knee

photos.caption: Holding the twist
photos.alt: Seated Spinal Twist: holding the twist

steps: Sit tall with legs straight in front of you.
Bend your right knee and place your right foot outside your left knee.
Breathe in to lengthen your spine, then breathe out and rotate toward your right knee.
Hug the knee with your left arm, place your right hand behind you, and hold.
Unwind slowly and repeat on the other side.
tips: Grow taller on each in-breath and twist a little more on each out-breath.
Keep both sitting bones grounded.

neck-stretch.name: Side Neck Stretch
neck-stretch.summary: A gentle stretch for the sides of the neck and upper shoulders.

photos.caption: Standing tall
photos.alt: Side Neck Stretch: standing tall

photos.caption: Tilting the ear toward the shoulder
photos.alt: Side Neck Stretch: tilting the ear toward the shoulder

steps: Sit or stand tall with shoulders relaxed.
Slowly tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder.
For a little more stretch, rest your right hand lightly on your head.
Hold for the planned time, then return to centre and switch sides.
tips: Keep the opposite shoulder down.
Never pull hard on your head; let gravity do most of the work.

side-plank.name: Side Plank
side-plank.summary: A side-lying hold that strengthens the obliques and hip stabilisers.

photos.caption: Lying on one side
photos.alt: Side Plank: lying on one side

photos.caption: Hips lifted into the side plank
photos.alt: Side Plank: hips lifted into the side plank

steps: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and legs stacked.
Brace your core and lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Hold for the planned time while breathing steadily.
Lower your hips slowly, then repeat on the other side.
tips: Drop the bottom knee to the floor for an easier version.
Keep your top hip stacked over the bottom hip rather than rolling forward.

single-leg-balance.name: Single-Leg Balance
single-leg-balance.summary: Standing on one leg to improve balance, ankle stability and core control.

photos.caption: Standing on one leg with knee lifted
photos.alt: Single-Leg Balance: standing on one leg with knee lifted

photos.caption: Tree pose variation
photos.alt: Single-Leg Balance: tree pose variation

steps: Stand tall near a wall or chair for support if needed.
Shift your weight onto one foot and lift the other foot off the floor.
Keep your standing knee soft and your hips level.
Hold for the planned time, breathing steadily, then switch legs.
tips: Fix your gaze on a point in front of you to steady yourself.
To progress, place the lifted foot on your inner calf (tree pose) or close your eyes briefly.

calf-stretch.name: Standing Calf Stretch
calf-stretch.summary: A wall stretch for the calf muscles and Achilles tendon.

photos.caption: Leaning into the wall
photos.alt: Standing Calf Stretch: leaning into the wall

photos.caption: Back heel pressed down
photos.alt: Standing Calf Stretch: back heel pressed down

steps: Stand facing a wall with your hands on it at shoulder height.
Step one foot back and keep that leg straight with the heel on the floor.
Bend the front knee and lean toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.
Hold for the planned time, then switch legs.
tips: Point both feet straight ahead.
Bend the back knee slightly to shift the stretch lower into the calf.

calf-raise.name: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise
calf-raise.summary: A simple rise onto the toes that strengthens the calves and ankles.

photos.caption: Starting position
photos.alt: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise: starting position

photos.caption: Finishing position
photos.alt: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise: finishing position

steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Breathe out and push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as you can.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower your heels slowly back to the floor.
tips: Stand near a wall and touch it lightly if you need balance.
Do the movement slowly; bouncing reduces the work for the calves.

treadmill-run.name: Treadmill Run / Jog
treadmill-run.summary: Jogging or running intervals to build cardiovascular fitness.

photos.caption: Running on the treadmill
photos.alt: Treadmill Run / Jog: running on the treadmill

photos.caption: Mid-stride
photos.alt: Treadmill Run / Jog: mid-stride

steps: Warm up with a few minutes of walking.
Increase the speed to a light jog or the planned running pace.
Land softly under your hips with short, quick steps and relaxed shoulders.
For intervals, alternate the faster pace with slow walking as planned.
Finish with a few minutes of walking to cool down.
tips: A comfortable steady pace lets you speak in short sentences.
Learn where the stop button or safety clip is before speeding up.

treadmill-walk.name: Treadmill Walk
treadmill-walk.summary: Steady walking for warm-ups, cool-downs and easy cardio.

photos.caption: Walking at an easy pace
photos.alt: Treadmill Walk: walking at an easy pace

photos.caption: Upright posture on the treadmill
photos.alt: Treadmill Walk: upright posture on the treadmill

steps: Step onto the side rails and start the belt at a slow speed.
Step on and walk, then raise the speed to the planned pace (easy: about 3–4 km/h; brisk: 4–5 km/h).
Stand tall, swing your arms naturally and look ahead.
Slow the belt gradually for the last minute before stopping.
tips: Avoid holding the handrails, which changes your posture.
At an easy pace you should be able to hold a conversation.

tricep-kickback.name: Tricep Kickback
tricep-kickback.summary: A one-arm extension that isolates the back of the upper arm.

photos.caption: Starting position
photos.alt: Tricep Kickback: starting position

photos.caption: Finishing position
photos.alt: Tricep Kickback: finishing position

steps: Place your left knee and left hand on a bench so your back is flat and roughly parallel to the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with your upper arm tucked against your side and elbow bent to 90°.
Breathe out and straighten your elbow, pushing the dumbbell back until your arm is straight.
Pause, then bend the elbow to return to the start.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
tips: Keep the upper arm fixed — only the forearm moves.
Keep your neck in line with your spine; look at the floor just ahead of the bench.
